name: Determining When a Student Fails a Course (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that determines whether a student fails the course based on the inputs that it receives from the instructor. The student fails the course if the exam score is less than 55 or when the student has cheated.
code:
#Step 1: Read the instructor inputs
text = input("Enter the exam score:")
exam_score = int(text)
text = input("Enter 1 if the student has cheated, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 2: Determine whether the student has cheated
if input_num == 1 :
    has_cheated = True
else:
    has_cheated = False
#Step 3: Write the boolean expression to determine whether the student fails the course
is_failing = exam_score < 55 or has_cheated
#Step 4: Print the result
if is_failing == True :
    print("Yes! The student fails the course.")
else:
    print("No! The student does not fail the course.")

commentList: You use this line to show the prompt Enter the exam score: to the instructor and capture whatever they type into the variable text so you can use it later.

You call the built-in function input(...) with a prompt string; input(...) waits for the user to type and press Enter, then returns that value as a string. The = operator stores that returned string in the variable text.

Be careful: input(...) always returns text, not a number. You might expect a numeric value here, but the conversion to an integer happens on the next line (exam_score = int(text)). If the instructor types letters, an empty string, or a decimal like 72.5, int(text) will raise an error.

To avoid common mistakes, you should validate what the user typed before converting. For example, you can strip whitespace, check that the string contains only digits (or handle a sign), or wrap int(text) in a try/except block and re-prompt until the instructor enters a valid whole-number score.

As a best practice, use a clearer variable name (for example score_input or exam_text) and make the prompt more specific (for example Enter the exam score (0-100):) so the instructor knows the expected format.
